newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says peso slump likely to be temporary.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says peso slump likely to be temporary.

text.p: The Philippines Central Bank on Friday said the plunge in the peso was likely to be temporary.
But in a statement it made clear that a main reason for loosening its hold on the peso was that it was using up too much money in its defence.
"We are not really devaluing the peso...we have decided to simply allow the peso to move within a new wider range consistent with a market-determined exchange rate policy," it said in a statement.
"Under current circumstances this has led to a depreciation of the peso but we expect this temporary situation to stabilise as the market is invariably self-correcting."
The bank said its main concern was to protect Philippine economic gains from turbulence in the region's currency market.
"We are not pre-judging what the exchange rate should be...we are allowing the market to find its own balance," it said, adding a more flexible exchange policy would keep speculators at bay.

It estimated that foreign currency reserves had plunged to $10 billion, about $2.5 billion down from March when the Philippines first began to be hit by concerns it was following in the footsteps of Thailand's economic crisis.
